newsitem.title: USA: Coastal sells coal units for $615 million.
newsitem.headline: Coastal sells coal units for $615 million.

text.p: Coastal Corp. said Thursday it agreed to sell its western coal operations for $615 million in cash to a company jointly owned by Atlantic Richfield Co. and Itochu Corp. of Japan.
The operations being sold consist of Coastal's three Utah mines and a 9 percent interest in Los Angeles Export Terminal Co. Inc., it said.
The company said it will retain its ANR Coal Co. subsidiary operating primarily in the eastern United States.
Coastal said it "expects to record a significant gain on the transaction."
Atlantic Richfield said it will have a 65 percent stake in the underground coal mines, and Itochu a 35 percent interest.
Arco Coal Co., a division of Arco, will manage the new company.

Arco said the mines -- SUFCO, Skyline and Soldier Creek -- are located in Utah's Uinta Basin and produce 10 million tons per year of low sulphur, high BTU bituminous coal which is sold to power plants and industrial users in the United States, Japan and other Asian countries.
The mines are estimated to contain 300 million tons of coal reserves.

"Arco Coal's interest in the newly formed company enhances our position as one of the premier producers and marketers of western low sulphur coal," said Michael DeGenring, Acting President of Denver-based Arco Coal.
"Itochu has unique marketing expertise in Japan and elsewhere in the Pacific Rim, which will be quite valuable as our new company explores additional potential markets," he said.
Tokyo-based Itochu has been the main trading channel since the early 1980s for the export of Coastal's western coal into the Japanese power utility and steel mill market.
The sale is expected to be completed by year-end.
Coastal's stock was off 12.5 cents at $45, and Arco was off $1.50 at $132.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
